title: SSC CHSL Tier 2 Descriptive — 14 Feb 2021
subTitle: Official Descriptive Paper (Pen & Paper Mode, 100 Marks)

questions.questionText:
Write an essay in English on the following topic:
"Freedom of Speech in India: Constitutional Provisions and Public Debate"
questions.explanation: Descriptive writing evaluation based on relevance, structure, vocabulary, and argument coherence.
questions.modelSolution:
Freedom of speech and expression is one of the foundational pillars of Indian democracy, guaranteed under Article 19(1)(a) of
the Constitution of India. It empowers citizens to participate actively in democratic governance, express opinions, critique
policies, and hold authority accountable.
However, this liberty is not absolute. Recognizing the delicate balance between personal freedom and societal harmony, the
Constitution outlines reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2). These restrictions apply on grounds including the sovereignty
and integrity of India, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign nations, public order, decency, morality, and
defamation.
In recent years, public debate surrounding free speech has intensified, catalyzed largely by the digital revolution. Social media
platforms have democratized information sharing, allowing marginalized voices to be heard instantly. Conversely, they have
also amplified hate speech, misinformation, and communal polarization. The debate today often centers on where legitimate
dissent ends and criminal incitement begins.
A mature democracy requires constructive debate, tolerance for divergent perspectives, and responsible expression. Citizens
must exercise self-restraint while authorities must ensure that statutory restrictions are invoked strictly within constitutional
parameters, preserving this vital democratic freedom.
rubrics: Relevance to Topic & Conceptual Clarity (15 Marks)
Structure, Coherence & Flow of Ideas (15 Marks)
Adherence to Word Limit & Format Guidelines (10 Marks)

questions.questionText:
You are Suresh, resident of House No. 323, Devnagar, Delhi, a tribal activist living in Delhi. Write a letter
to the District Authority (SDM/Collector), Bastar, Chhattisgarh, highlighting the problems faced by the
tribal community and requesting prompt administrative intervention.
questions.explanation: Formal letter evaluation based on official format, civic address, conciseness, and tone.
questions.modelSolution:
House No. 323, Devnagar,
Delhi - 110007.

14th February, 2021.

The District Magistrate / Collector,
Bastar District,
Chhattisgarh.

Subject: Urgent administrative intervention regarding welfare and livelihood challenges of tribal communities.

Respected Sir/Madam,

I am writing to draw your urgent attention to the pressing socioeconomic issues faced by the tribal communities residing in the remote blocks of Bastar district.

Despite diverse welfare schemes, local tribal settlements continue to face acute difficulties in accessing primary healthcare facilities and clean drinking water, especially during seasonal transitions. Moreover, the procurement mechanism for Minor Forest Produce (MFP) requires streamlined operationalization to guarantee minimum support prices without middleman exploitation.

I earnestly request your good office to organize mobile medical units in underserved gram panchayats and establish dedicated local grievance redressal camps. Timely administrative intervention will ensure that constitutional safeguards and development welfare effectively reach the grassroots indigenous population.

Thanking you.

Yours faithfully,
Suresh
(Tribal Rights Activist)
